notes: GeneReviews CADASIL was reread on 2026-08-27. It directly supports migraine with aura, recurrent subcortical ischemic events, anterior temporal/external-capsule white-matter hyperintensities, autosomal dominant inheritance, characteristic granular osmiophilic material, and mutant NOTCH3 extracellular-domain aggregation with vascular smooth-muscle-cell degeneration.
MedlinePlus NOTCH3 and CADASIL pages were reread and independently support the NOTCH3/vascular-smooth-muscle-cell mechanism and autosomal dominant inheritance.
NCBI/MedlinePlus sources were reread for cerebral amyloid angiopathy, COL4A1-related small-vessel disease, MELAS, and Wilson disease to verify all four distractor mechanisms.
The official USMLE Content Outline 2026 was visually inspected at Nervous System & Special Senses page 9; cerebrovascular disease is an explicit outline category.

blueprint.system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
blueprint.competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts

duplicate_gate.rejected_candidate_note: Syringomyelia was rejected after a broader semantic gate found real overlap with canonical Q0420 testing the anterior white commissure/spinothalamic crossing.

claim_audit.phenotype: GeneReviews supports migraine with aura, recurrent ischemic stroke/TIA, lacunes/subcortical infarcts, and symmetric white-matter hyperintensities often involving the anterior temporal lobes and external capsules.
claim_audit.inheritance: GeneReviews and MedlinePlus support autosomal dominant inheritance caused by heterozygous pathogenic NOTCH3 variants.
claim_audit.molecular_mechanism: GeneReviews states that pathogenic variants commonly create an unpaired cysteine in an EGFr domain, disrupt disulfide-bond formation, cause aggregation of mutant NOTCH3 extracellular domain, and have toxic effects leading to vascular smooth-muscle-cell degeneration.
claim_audit.pathology: GeneReviews states that skin-biopsy electron microscopy can show granular osmiophilic material in vascular media close to vascular smooth muscle cells.
claim_audit.distractor_1: Cerebral amyloid angiopathy is correctly represented as amyloid-beta deposition in cortical/leptomeningeal vessels causing vessel fragility and a lobar hemorrhagic phenotype; it does not match this young-adult CADASIL pattern.
claim_audit.distractor_2: COL4A1-related disease is a real autosomal dominant cerebral small-vessel disorder caused by abnormal type IV collagen and vascular fragility, making it a plausible distractor; however the CADASIL-specific migraine/family/MRI constellation points to NOTCH3.
claim_audit.distractor_3: MELAS is a mitochondrial disorder with impaired oxidative phosphorylation and stroke-like episodes, commonly maternally inherited, not the paternal autosomal-dominant pattern shown.
claim_audit.distractor_4: Wilson disease is caused by ATP7B dysfunction with copper accumulation in liver and brain and a different neurologic/hepatic phenotype.
claim_audit.blueprint_claim: Official USMLE Content Outline 2026 places cerebrovascular disease within Nervous System & Special Senses.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: A young adult with migraine with aura, recurrent focal ischemic symptoms, multiple lacunar infarcts, anterior temporal/external-capsule white-matter disease, and successive affected relatives on one parental lineage strongly indicates an autosomal dominant cerebral small-vessel arteriopathy. The characteristic disorder is CADASIL, and its foundational molecular lesion is mutant NOTCH3 extracellular-domain aggregation with vascular smooth-muscle-cell degeneration.
adversarial_second_pass.col4a1_challenge: COL4A1 disease can be autosomal dominant and can cause migraine, white-matter disease, and stroke, so it is a serious distractor. However COL4A1 more characteristically causes fragile-vessel/hemorrhagic phenotypes and may include ocular, renal, muscle, or developmental findings. The anterior temporal/external-capsule MRI pattern plus CADASIL clinical constellation makes NOTCH3 uniquely best.
adversarial_second_pass.caa_challenge: CAA can cause focal neurologic events and white-matter abnormalities, but sporadic CAA is strongly age-related and typically presents with lobar hemorrhagic lesions; the 38-year-old autosomal-dominant CADASIL pattern is incompatible.
adversarial_second_pass.melas_challenge: MELAS causes stroke-like episodes before age 40, but mitochondrial inheritance is maternal and systemic mitochondrial findings such as lactic acidosis, seizures, hearing loss, or myopathy would be expected. The paternal transmission pattern directly argues against mtDNA disease.
adversarial_second_pass.wilson_challenge: Wilson disease can present in young adults with neurologic disease, but ATP7B copper accumulation produces hepatic, movement, psychiatric, and ocular findings rather than an inherited lacunar small-vessel syndrome.
adversarial_second_pass.wording_challenge: The lead asks for the molecular mechanism rather than diagnosis. The correct option states the supported pathogenic aggregate/VSMC mechanism and does not merely restate NOTCH3 as a gene-name recall.
adversarial_second_pass.cueing_check: All five options are mechanistic statements of similar length and specificity. The CAA distractor was explicitly shortened/corrected before final audit to remove an unnecessary and potentially misleading APP-processing qualifier.
adversarial_second_pass.unsupported_precision_check: The item uses no unsupported penetrance, prevalence, fixed age cutoff, MRI sensitivity, or mutation-frequency percentages. Age and family-history details are contextual rather than asserted diagnostic thresholds.
